description:
We don't just howl at the Moon; we make it work for the fields! Turning NASA's cosmic data into down-to-earth innovations, we're here to help farmers adapt, thrive, and harvest a brighter future.

Come night or day, may the moonlight connect us.
summary:
AniTala is a web app that helps Philippine farmers explore crop-rotation plans. Farmers tap their field on a map or pick a pilot town, confirm soil details, set priorities like profit, water saving, and storm toughness, and receive ranked plans for the wet, cool-dry, and hot-dry seasons, printable or shareable in English or Filipino.
It combines NASA POWER’s 10-year climate record and NASA GIBS satellite layers (true color and vegetation greenness) with global soil data, crop traits, and each farmer’s priorities. Plans are scored with transparent rules, and what-if tests (hotter, drier, wetter) show whether a plan holds up as weather and water conditions change. Shifting temperatures, erratic rainfall, and declining soil health make rotation choices harder for smallholders, who rarely have locally tailored advice. AniTala turns Earth observation data into plain-language, explainable guidance that supports soil health and resilience. It is decision support, not a yield forecast, and currently covers four pilot municipalities.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

AniTala (from the Filipino words "Ani" [harvest] and "Tala" [guiding star]) is a zero-auth, mobile-first agricultural decision-support web application designed for smallholder farmers and municipal agricultural extension workers in the Philippines. It transforms space agency Earth observation records into tailored, resilient 3-season crop rotation schedules.

How It Works:

  1. Interactive Field Location & Satellite Overlays: Farmers select their agricultural area (calibrated across four pilot municipal hubs: Science City of Muñoz, City of Ilagan, Pototan, and Malaybalay City). Interactive Leaflet maps stream real-time satellite imagery via NASA GIBS WMTS (MODIS Terra True Color optical imagery and 8-day NDVI vegetation greenness).
    • NASA POWER Daily Point API: Ingests 10 complete calendar years (3,652 daily observations) of localized agroclimatology to compute seasonal rainfall normals, peak heat stress days (T_max≥34^∘C and ≥35^∘C ), solar irradiance, and dry-spell runs.
    • ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0: Automatically retrieves modeled topsoil physical properties (sand, silt, and clay fractions, soil pH, and soil organic carbon).
    • One-Tap Farmer Soil Override: Acknowledging that satellite and digital models are estimates, farmers can tap to override soil texture and pH based on physical ground truth or municipal soil test kits.
    • Monsoon Cropping Calendar: Sequences are mapped across the tropical Philippine cycle: Wet Season / Habagat (June–October), Cool Dry Season / Amihan (November–February), and Hot Dry Season / Tag-init (March–May).
    • Hard Agronomic Constraints: Eliminates continuous monocultures, prohibits consecutive Solanaceous crops (e.g., Tomato →\to→ Eggplant) to break devastating soil-borne bacterial wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) and root-knot nematodes, and prevents unbuffered grass-to-grass sequences.
    • Five-Pillar Agronomic Scoring (0–100): Scores valid sequences across Soil Health (biological nitrogen fixation bonuses fixing 35–80 kg N/ha, root depth stratification), Water Resilience (monsoon flood buffering and dry-season drought defense), Climate Shock Buffer, Economic Viability (staple security, input costs, market tiers), and Labor Feasibility.
  2. Climate Shock Stress-Testing: Evaluates all generated sequences against 5 climate shock scenarios: Baseline, Hotter (+1.5°C), Drier (-15% rainfall / El Niño), Hotter + Drier Compound Shock, and Wetter (+15% intense monsoon / typhoons). Sequences that maintain rank and stability receive the "Climate-Robust" certification.
  3. Printable Advisory & Actionable Explanations: Every plan includes transparent rule tags (e.g., [AGRO-RULE-01-NFIX]), exact telemetry citations, identified operational risks (e.g., heat flower abortion), and concrete mitigations (e.g., rice-straw mulching), with a 1-page printable advisory sheet (Ctrl+P) ready for field distribution.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Breaks Destructive Pest & Disease Cycles: Enforces strict botanical family separation, preventing the recurring crop failures smallholders face from soil-borne pathogens when planting continuous cash crops.
  • Natural Soil Fertility & Lower Input Costs: Strategically slots biological nitrogen-fixing legumes (mungbean, peanut, cowpea) after heavy-feeding grains (rice, corn), restoring soil organic matter and significantly lowering chemical fertilizer expenses.
  • De-risks Extreme Weather Events: Identifies heat-tolerant and drought-hardy transition crops, shielding farmers from devastating compound El Niño heatwaves or unexpected monsoon shifts.
  • Bilingual & Field-Accessible: Farmers and extension technicians can seamlessly switch between English and Filipino / Tagalog with a mobile-optimized UI designed for low-bandwidth rural connectivity.
  • 100% Explainable ("Glass-Box"): Gives clear agronomic justifications with exact satellite numbers instead of obscure black-box recommendations, building essential trust with farmers.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Empowering Grassroots Climate Adaptation: Shifts rural climate response from reactive disaster relief to proactive, season-by-season agronomic adaptation.
  • Equipping Municipal Extension Workers: Bridges the technological gap for Municipal Agriculture Offices (LGU-MAO) and agricultural technicians by giving them a zero-install tool to generate data-backed rotation advisories for their farming communities.
  • Improving Farm Household Incomes: Protects smallholder livelihoods from total seasonal loss by balancing household staple food security (rice/corn) with high-value cash crops and low-input fertility crops.
  • Democratizing Space Telemetry: Proves that complex multi-terabyte NASA Earth observation archives can be distilled into straightforward, usable guidance on a smartphone screen without requiring accounts, logins, or paid subscriptions.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend & Core Framework: React 19, TypeScript, Vite (Rolldown bundler).
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS v4 (custom mobile-first design system with high-contrast sunlight outdoor legibility).
  • Mapping & GIS: Leaflet with NASA GIBS Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) WMTS tile integration and OpenStreetMap.
  • Data Validation & State Management: Zod (runtime telemetry schema validation) and Zustand (reactive client state).
  • Data Visualizations & Icons: Recharts (10-year monthly precipitation and temperature curves) and Lucide React.
  • Testing & Quality Assurance: Vitest (comprehensive unit test suite verifying deterministic engine scoring, climate shocks, and contrast ratios) and Oxlint (high-performance static linting).
  • Data Preprocessing & Offline ETL: Python 3 (Rasterio, NumPy) for pre-bundling offline digital soil GeoTIFF fallbacks.
  • Hosting & Infrastructure: Deployed as a zero-auth static web application on Vercel with IndexedDB and localStorage caching for resilient offline field operation.

5. How is your project creative?

  • "Glass-Box" Deterministic Agronomy over Black-Box AI: In high-stakes subsistence agriculture, an AI model that cannot explain why it recommended a crop will be rejected. AniTala's creativity lies in encoding peer-reviewed agronomic principles (biological nitrogen fixation, root depth stratification, bacterial disease breaks) into a pure TypeScript engine that produces cited, human-auditable reasons for every score.
  • Stress-Testing Rotations like Financial Portfolios: We adapted financial stress-testing principles into agronomy: treating a 3-season crop rotation as an investment portfolio subjected to compounding climate shocks (Hotter, Drier, Wetter, Compound).
  • Bridging Space Telemetry with Farmer Ground Truth: Instead of dictating soil conditions from satellite estimates, AniTala pairs satellite and global soil models with an immediate Farmer Override mechanism—honoring local traditional knowledge alongside orbital data.
  • Cultural Design & Dual Identity: Inspired by the Filipino tradition of looking to the stars to guide seasonal planting, the UI combines native agricultural imagery with functional field utilities (high sunlight contrast, single-page print layouts).

6. What factors did your team consider?

  1. Outdoor Field Usability & Connectivity:
    • Farmers work outdoors under bright tropical sunlight on budget smartphones. We strictly enforced WCAG AA / AAA contrast standards (4.5:1 to 13.7:1) across all text, dark green banners, and controls.
    • Built a resilient 3-tier fallback architecture (Live API →\to→ Persistent 7-Day Local Cache →\to→ Pre-bundled Offline Fixtures) so the app works even when mobile signal drops in remote barangays.
    • NASA POWER has a 0.5° (~55 km) grid and SoilGrids has a 250 m resolution. We explicitly framed all outputs as advisory decision support, not rigid yield predictions, openly disclosing satellite uncertainty.
    • Requiring NASA Earthdata accounts, passwords, or paid API keys would immediately exclude smallholders. The entire application is 100% zero-auth and runs directly in any modern mobile browser.
    • Refused to make generic national claims. Calibrated the pilot strictly to four distinct agro-ecological zones (Central Luzon lowland rice plains, Cagayan Valley corn river basins, Iloilo drought-prone rainfed paddies, and Bukidnon volcanic high plateaus).
    • Maintained bilingual parity across all UI strings, scientific disclosures, and rule explanations in English and Filipino / Tagalog.
